The plan is committed and pushed: /home/user/ps-s-shell/docs/studio-overhaul/shell-plan.md, commit e951c09 on claude/studio-shell. Only that file is in the commit. No code was changed.

Profiling done for the plan (scratchpad script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/8d80c188-0981-544b-8b2d-c9de04f0705c/scratchpad/shell-plan/poolprof.ts, vite-node, desktop CPU, run through heavy.sh):

| Step | NBA | NFL | Soccer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Card file imported as a JS object literal (how Vite 5.4.10 emits JSON today) | 1,531 ms | 1,158 ms | 1,987 ms |
| Same file through JSON.parse | 21 ms | 20 ms | 36 ms |
| expandCards (one synchronous call) | 178 ms | 279 ms | 151 ms |
| Rating every line | 1,103 ms | 1,060 ms | 109 ms |

So `json.stringify` plus sliced expand removes the 385-669 ms long tasks. Getting under 2.5 s at 4x CPU still needs the per-build rated-pool cache and Home-idle prefetch (shell-7). I chose a runtime cache keyed by app version over build-time precomputed ratings because four teams are changing rating code in parallel.

Decisions for the lead:
- **Production builds for measurement.** The service worker and precache only exist in production builds, so shell-6 to shell-9 each need at most one `heavy.sh npx vite build --manifest --outDir <scratchpad>` (not `npm run build`). - **Protocol:** no bump is expected from shell. The UT queue guard, pool.print, is proven unchanged by tests in shell-6 and shell-7. DRAFT_RULES and UT_RULES are never touched.

Revised plan committed and pushed: /home/user/ps-s-shell/docs/studio-overhaul/shell-plan.md (commit 68123cc on claude/studio-shell). §9 of the plan maps all 74 critique points (22 missing, 12 restructure, 20 risks, 20 targets) to a task, or gives the reason for a partial acceptance or rejection.

Verified in code before revising:
- No error boundary exists in src.
- Arcade.tsx:155-164 loaders have no .catch.
- Training.tsx:209/229 and Moments.tsx:74/84 mount engines directly.
- All three engines createPortal .arcade-full into document.body at z 50. So arena.ts uses a cheap non-subtree body childList observer, and the arena already paints over the status plate.
- #root is position:fixed with no z-index, so the plate covers in-root overlays. Hence the overlay-aware plate: UT colour, scrim composite #030c10, hidden on immersive screens.
- Raw env() top rules exist in ut CSS (clubhouse.css:1366, content-ui.css:1021/1038) and in unowned evolution.css. Its .save-warning banner sits in the blur band.
- Cloud archive runs only on conflict (cloud-sync.ts:240), so an erase can't be recovered from the server.
- On the 9-device matrix, Home's room after the edge is 731.4-744 frame px on island and notch phones, just above the 730 snug threshold (393: +1.4, 420: +1.7, 402: +3.4). Home's class therefore reads the raw room.

Partly accepted or rejected, with reasons in the plan:
- Requiring cloud status 'saved' before ERASE: replaced by a state-worded acknowledgement plus lead decision D7, because 'saved' doesn't make an erase recoverable and it blocks offline players.
- Cold UT open <=3,500 ms at 4×: rejected as a shell acceptance, because rating alone costs 4.2-4.4 s at 4× in packs-owned code. The plan sets <=6,000 ms and asks the lead for sign-off (D6).
- Lie-fi relaunch <=1,100 ms: set to NAV_TIMEOUT + 600 ms, with the timeout tuned by a no-loop test.
- Navigation preload: dropped, because it ignores cache:'no-cache' and risks update loops.
- In-game latency and game-clock targets: shell measures and reports them; the sport and players teams own the fixes.
- Splitting shell-10 into four tasks: kept as parts A/B/C because of the 10-task cap. The harnesses are spread into the tasks that use them, and the audit's isolated matchperf.cjs replaces a new port.
